title: Soul Snack #40: How Do I Change My Self-Destructive Behaviors?
excerpt: Are you creating with love or fear in your life?
bodyHtml:
Are you creating with love or fear in your life? Take this self-assessment today to find out.

In this powerful Soul Snack, Gary Zukav responds to a heartfelt listener question about navigating overwhelming life circumstances and coping through cannabis use. The listener shares her journey of raising a son with quadriplegia, born after an intrauterine stroke, and her struggle with self-medication.

With deep compassion, Gary explores how to begin releasing self-destructive behaviors by seeing beyond victimhood and awakening to the deeper spiritual meaning behind our challenges.

At the heart of this Soul Snack is the invitation to shift from identifying with fear-based parts of our personality to aligning with our soul’s intentions to create harmony, cooperation, sharing and reverence for Life.

Gary shares that even the most painful, persistent emotional states – like overwhelm, despair, or addictive cravings – are opportunities to create authentic power by choosing awareness, presence, and love.

This episode encourages listeners to recognize every life experience, no matter how difficult, as part of a soul agreement offering profound growth.

The path out of self-destruction begins by honoring the pain without numbing it, and instead choosing to respond with gratitude, appreciation, and responsibility.
Healing starts by seeing yourself – and those around you – as powerful souls in Earth school, walking a journey of transformation.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Snack:

(00:40) – The listener’s story: parenting a child with special needs and coping with emotional overwhelm through cannabis
(01:12) – Why seeing yourself as a victim is inaccurate—and how this belief limits your power
(02:41) – A spiritual perspective: your child as a soul who chose this path and brings gifts into your life
(03:40) – How to recognize fear-based parts of your personality and shift toward love-based responses
(04:34) – Practical ways to respond to overwhelm with awareness instead of distraction or addiction
(05:30) – How deep soul connection and spiritual responsibility can transform your sense of self

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge:

Reflect on a moment when you turned to distraction – like substances, overwork, or emotional withdrawal – to avoid inner pain. What sensations arose in your body? Can you identify the frightened part of your personality seeking comfort or escape? Instead of numbing the experience, take time to feel it fully. Then, reach for the healthiest, most loving part of yourself. Imagine being grateful – for your child, your challenges, or simply for the opportunity to grow. Ask yourself: What would it feel like to respond with love rather than fear?
